evidence: Every instance reviewed: 2 gate criteria, 15 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual. MOSTLY STRONG. (1) Gates: hro_gate_render requires a refused wrong password plus a positive sign-in into a populated workspace; hro_gate_shared requires a UI-added uniquely named card that survives reload and is found exactly once by the Observer in an independent context - browser outcome, durable, distinctive. (2) Functional (tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:27-160): every criterion uses suffixed fresh jobs/cards, grades concrete DOM/network outcomes (orders, stages, HTTP 401/403/404/409, document.activeElement, response bodies searched for a unique rejection-reason suffix), pairs refusals with same-kind controls (functional prompt.md:17,25) and re-reads state after refusals. Seeded facts quoted are correct against seed_data.json: Platform Engineer Applied Greta Lindqvist, Ade Bello, Marco Rossi and Screen Priya Nair, Samuel Ortiz; APP-101 note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.'; APP-101 holds 120 messages numbered (#001...) so 'none missing or repeated' is decidable; Lena's APP-301 has 3 messages with read_count 2, so unread 1; Noor PE = INTERVIEW (Interviewing), Noor PD = APPLIED, Tomas DA = SCREEN (In review). Multi-card order expectations re-derived and self-consistent (hro_bulk: Y,W,X below V; A2,V; Z first in board order in step 4, V last in step 8; hro_undo: Applied Y,W,X,Z,A2 after the undo). Restart (hro_intake_restart) records several distinct items (two jobs, per-stage orders, a rejection with reason, a note, a message, unread total, Activity lines, the seeded order and note) and re-reads them in a fresh context after restart_app (lesson 15), compared against the pre-restart baseline (lesson 16). hro_two_people's exact replay after Mei moves F back to Applied is a distinctive ABA probe consistent with hireops_rules.md section 3 ('every card carries a version that changes whenever the card moves'). (3) Lessons 7/14 timing void/repeat: functional prompt.md:29 and polish prompt.md:18 define one browser_run_code_unsafe action per timed observation, t0 only after the trigger succeeded, void = errored before t0 or trigger failed, at most two repeats, met=false final, all-void fails, negatives watched for the full window and confirmed in a fresh independent context. Every timed step references it: hro_two_people step 2, hro_messaging step 1, hro_long_thread (two), hro_unread_seen steps 3-5, hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread (60 s via 'or the longer watch a criterion names'; polish prompt.md:14 'Each live row is one timed observation'). Lesson 8 modifier hold is in app_context.md:33-35; lesson 9 step reporting in functional prompt.md:31-33 and polish prompt.md:20-22. test.sh:207 runs judges with --max-concurrent-agent 1, so watched counts are not disturbed by concurrent sessions. (4) Visual: five likert craft rows with five described anchors each; subjective but anchored and sanctioned by row 41 - Note only. DEFECT (one instance): polish hro_pol_earlier_place (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:65-72): 'scroll to the top of what is shown and note which message is at the top of the view and its position (getBoundingClientRect().top). Bring in earlier messages. The same message stays at the same position on screen'. The brief leaves the loading mechanism to the builder ('lets me pull in earlier ones without losing my place'; hireops_rules.md section 6 'I bring in earlier messages 30 at a time'), so scroll-triggered auto-loading is a conforming design. For such an app the probe is not decidable as written: scrolling to the top IS the load, so the noted position is taken before or after the load depending on tool-call timing, and if after, the judge's further scroll to the top to 'bring in earlier messages' moves the noted message by its own scroll, so a correct position-preserving app can be read as 'jumped'. The golden (threads.js:15,161-172) uses an explicit button outside the scroll log, so it is unaffected and the scripted golden evidence does not exercise the alternative. No other instance of 'looks right', a source read, a response-shape-only assertion, or a trace-less probe found. Minor notes (not defects): hro_long_thread reads the open conversation's unread count, which a layout hiding the list while a thread is open makes harder, but network data is allowed; an app that dedups exact replays by request id would not return 409 in hro_two_people, but the brief requires the version refusal. NOT EXERCISED: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'), so judge behaviour under these protocols is unmeasured.
counterexample: A conforming app whose conversation loads the previous 30 messages automatically when the list is scrolled to the top and keeps the previously top message fixed (scrollTop += added height). The judge scrolls to the top (the load fires and completes before its next tool call), notes message M at position p, finds no 'earlier' control, scrolls to the top again to bring in more; M moves down by the judge's own scroll and the next batch loads above. The judge compares M with p, sees a large shift and fails hro_pol_earlier_place (weight 2 of 9.5 in polish, about 4% of total reward) for a correct app.
suggested_fix: Add to hro_pol_earlier_place: 'If earlier messages load on their own when the list reaches the top, do it in one browser_run_code_unsafe action: set the list's scrollTop to 0 (or wheel up), immediately record the top-most visible message and its getBoundingClientRect().top, wait until the message count rises, and compare that same message's top without scrolling again.'
